record.context_brief: Information geometry for generalized-mean quantum Fisher metrics
record.original_question: When quantum Fisher metrics are generated from generalized means, is there an information-geometric framework that can treat the resulting variety of metrics in a unified way?

evidence.quote: In quantum information theory, the variety of the quantum Fisher metric is introduced by using the generalized mean [13]. Is there a framework for treating this variety in information geometry?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ denote the manifold of faithful density operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$. A monotone (quantum Fisher) Riemannian metric on $\mathcal{S}$ is, by Petz's classification, in one-to-one correspondence with an operator monotone function $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ satisfying $f(1)=1$ and $f(t)=tf(1/t)$, via the formula
$$\langle A,B\rangle_\rho^f = \mathrm{Tr}\bigl(A^*\, c_f(L_\rho,R_\rho)^{-1}\, B\bigr),\qquad c_f(x,y)=y\,f(x/y),$$
where $L_\rho$ and $R_\rho$ denote left and right multiplication by $\rho$, and $A,B$ are tangent vectors at $\rho$ (traceless self-adjoint operators). Each such $f$ corresponds to an operator mean $m_f(x,y)=c_f(x,y)$ in the sense of Kubo–Ando, and one obtains a wide variety of monotone metrics by choosing $f$ to be a "generalized mean" (e.g. arithmetic, geometric, harmonic, logarithmic, power means).

Problem: Construct an information-geometric framework — comprising a manifold structure, a family of (possibly non-symmetric) divergences, and a pair of dually coupled affine connections $(\nabla, \nabla^*)$ with respect to a Riemannian metric $g$ — that simultaneously realizes the entire family $\{\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle^f_\rho\}_f$ of generalized-mean quantum Fisher metrics on $\mathcal{S}$ as instances of a single unified construction, in such a way that the classical dualistic structure of Amari–Chentsov is recovered in commutative limits and the standard (SLD, BKM, right-logarithmic-derivative, geometric-mean) cases appear as distinguished members of the family.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal a substantial literature on monotone quantum Fisher metrics (Petz classification) and on partial dualistic structures associated with specific choices such as the SLD and BKM metrics, as well as recent work on generalized-mean Cramér–Rao bounds and "extended information geometry." However, no single source was found that provides a fully unified information-geometric framework covering the entire variety of generalized-mean quantum Fisher metrics, so the status of the problem as posed is inconclusive.

status_evidence.title: Fisher information metric - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum Fisher information is identified in information geometry with the SLD/Bures–Uhlmann metric.
status_evidence.claim: Standard quantum Fisher metrics have established information-geometric interpretations, but a unification across all generalized means is not described.

status_evidence.title: Extended Information Geometry Overview
status_evidence.snippet: Extended information geometry generalizes differential-geometric structures of classical information geometry to quantum models and non-Fisher divergences.
status_evidence.claim: General frameworks exist that extend information geometry beyond Fisher, but no specific unified treatment of generalized-mean quantum Fisher metrics is documented.

status_evidence.title: Quantum Fisher information matrix and multiparameter estimation
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized means including geometric and harmonic means yield corresponding Cramér–Rao bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Generalized-mean quantum Fisher metrics are studied individually for estimation, not unified geometrically.
